book_title: Isaf al-Talib fi Jami al-Matalib (The Student's Aid in All Demands)

preface.title: A Compiler's World: How to Read This Book

chapters.title: The Eight Levels of Faith
chapters.rationale: Opens the compiler's first book with the distinction between faith and Islam and the enumerated seven duties and twelve obligations.

chapters.title: Three Questions from the King of Rum
chapters.rationale: Gathers the narrative set-pieces in which Ali and al-Hasan answer the riddles that defeated others, establishing the Imams' inherited knowledge.

chapters.title: The Grammar of Peace
chapters.rationale: A self-contained unit on the seven divine and twelve human forms of the greeting of peace and how it must be returned.

chapters.title: Guardians, Proofs, and the Limits of Praise
chapters.rationale: Covers the houses and ranks of the Imams, their proofs and preachers, the ban on exaggeration, and their commandments to followers.

chapters.title: Parents, Kin, and the Neighbor at Your Side
chapters.rationale: The linked councils on love among believers, righteousness to spiritual and bodily parents, the twelve classes of kin, and the rights of neighbors.

chapters.title: What Must Be Learned, What Must Be Concealed
chapters.rationale: Runs from the duty to seek knowledge and the obligatory articles of belief to the ban on analogy and the command to guard the secret.

chapters.title: Water and Intention: The Anatomy of Ablution
chapters.rationale: Opens the Book of Purity with what nullifies ablution and the seven obligations and twelve Sunnahs of the lesser and greater purity.

chapters.title: The Manners of the Washing Place
chapters.rationale: Gathers the etiquette and detailed characteristics of ablution, including wounds, dried limbs, disputed water, and the inner meaning of the seven limbs.

chapters.title: Major Impurity and the Cleanliness of Things
chapters.rationale: Moves from ghusl for janabah to the purity of bodies, garments, ground, carpets, vessels, and the clothing of non-Muslims.

chapters.title: Tooth-Stick, Dust, and the Purity of Food
chapters.rationale: Covers the siwak, the law of purification by earth when water fails, and the purity of foods and drinks in the marketplace.

chapters.title: Bodies, Hair, and the Reform of Custom
chapters.rationale: Joins the rulings on circumcision, hair, and adornment with Jafar ibn Sulayman's letter rebuking the Indian and Yemeni innovations in these very practices.

chapters.title: Skins, Blood, and Waiting Periods
chapters.rationale: Covers the purity of skin, bone, hair, and wool, then menstruation and postpartum bleeding, closing the Book of Purity with istibra.

chapters.title: The Pillar of Religion and Its Appointed Hours
chapters.rationale: Opens the Book of Prayer with the virtues and neglect of prayer and the long treatment of prayer times, missed prayers, and repentance.

chapters.title: The Disputed Words of the Call
chapters.rationale: The call to prayer and the iqama, leading into the historical episode of al-Hakim and the contested phrase added to the adhan.

chapters.title: Eight Proofs for the Best of Human Beings
chapters.rationale: The complete epistolary debate defending the adhan formula through eight Quranic proofs and rebutting objections.

chapters.title: Where a Muslim Stands to Pray
chapters.rationale: A single thematic unit on mosques: their building, their graves, their greeting prayer, and the ranked merit of praying in each.

chapters.title: Who May Lead, and Who May Not
chapters.rationale: The conditions and disqualifications for leading prayer, followed by the rules of the congregation, its rows, and women's participation.

chapters.title: The Shape of the Prayer Itself
chapters.rationale: The obligatory acts and Sunnahs of prayer, including Jafar ibn Sulayman's rebuke of those who claim loyalty yet never prostrate.

chapters.title: Supplication, Speech, and Silence
chapters.rationale: The seven postures of supplication after prayer and the rulings on words, gestures, and bodily conduct within the prayer.

chapters.title: What the Worshipper Wears and Stands Upon
chapters.rationale: Garments, silk, figured carpets, covering of the awrah, and what surfaces may lawfully receive a prostration.

chapters.title: Friday and the Two Festivals
chapters.rationale: The Friday sermon and assembly together with the two Eid prayers, their takbirs, and the inner meaning of al-Fitr.

chapters.title: Forgetting, Doubting, and Beginning Again
chapters.rationale: The prostration of omission, the twelve cases of doubt, what interrupts prayer, and the prayer of the latecomer.

chapters.title: Children, Travelers, and the Sick
chapters.rationale: When boys are commanded to pray, the long law of the traveler's shortening and its exceptions, and the prayer of the incapacitated.

chapters.title: Eclipse, Fear, Rain, and the Night Vigil
chapters.rationale: The occasional and supererogatory prayers — eclipse, fear, istisqa, witr and qunut, Sunnah and nafl — closing with the prostration of Quranic recitation.

chapters.title: The Sickbed and the Sound of Mourning
chapters.rationale: Opens the Book of Funerals with visiting the sick, the remembrance of death, and the sharp condemnation of wailing over the dead.

chapters.title: Washing, Shrouding, Carrying, Burying
chapters.rationale: The sequence of rites for the corpse: washing, embalming and shroud, the procession, the funeral prayer, and the grave.

chapters.title: The Wealth That Is Not Yours
chapters.rationale: Opens the Book of Zakat with its intention, its seven sources and eight recipients, and the sin of withholding it from the Imam.

chapters.title: Gold, Herds, and Harvest
chapters.rationale: The detailed thresholds of zakat on gold and silver, on camels, cattle and sheep, and on grains, fruits, and mined wealth.

chapters.title: The Charity of the Head
chapters.rationale: Zakat al-fitr — its measure, its timing before the Eid prayer, and the residual cases of who owes nothing.

chapters.title: A Shield Against the Fire
chapters.rationale: Opens the Book of Fasting with the obligation of Ramadan and the seven obligatory and twelve recommended fasts.

chapters.title: The Quarrel Over the Crescent
chapters.rationale: The polemic arguing that Ramadan is never deficient and that fasting must not hang on the naked-eye sighting of the moon.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Sight
chapters.rationale: Al-Kirmani's epistle distinguishing sensory sight from the vision of knowledge and grounding the fast in calculated conjunction.

chapters.title: The Sun, the Moon, and the Order of Obedience
chapters.rationale: Concludes the epistle by answering the 'count thirty days' objection and reading the sun and moon as figures of the Prophet and his Foundation.
